Hi Laura / Chris,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the thoughtful questions. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

What we heard from you:
- Primary goal: replace your internal proprietary synth-response pipeline for customer help with an open-model stack to reduce hosting cost and avoid vendor lock-in.
- Key success metrics: intent classification >= 92% end-to-end, average resolution time under 1.8 turns, and human-annotator preference parity within 5 points vs baseline.
- Constraints: PII must never leave their VPC in production; sandbox data is fine for evaluation.

Redwood action items (what we'll deliver):
1) Evaluation bundle (by 2026-06-18): prompt sets + 500 representative test cases (see attached novus_eval_prompts.csv).
2) Baseline comparison spreadsheet with initial open-model vs proprietary baseline runs (baseline-comparison.xlsx).
3) Shortlist of recommended open models and quantization profiles + expected latency/cost tradeoffs.
4) Shared eval dashboard (link below) and a reproducible script to run the workloads in your sandbox.

Ask of Novus: please confirm the 500-case subset and nominate one engineering contact for sandbox access (we need a service account).

I'll loop Marissa in for the model recommendations and Neha for security checklist items.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Post-demo: initial notes + next steps for evals — recommended models and benchmarks

Hi team — following up with the recommended evaluation plan and concrete thresholds so Novus has something to approve/adjust quickly. Summary below; full runs and artifacts are in the Drive link.

Recommended model shortlist (open candidates):
- vicuna-13b-v1.5-q4f16 (fast, best cost/perf for short contexts)
- mixtral-8x7b-int8 (good long-context coherence)
- falcon-40b-instruct-8bit (strong instruction-following baseline)

Baseline (Novus proprietary): internal v2.4 (held by Novus).

Proposed automated metrics and acceptance thresholds:
- Intent accuracy (micro): >= 92% for the selected 500-case set.
- Turn-level resolution (avg conversational turns to resolved intent): <= 1.8.
- Human preference: difference (open model preferred % - baseline preferred %) >= -5 percentage points (i.e., up to 5 points worse acceptable provided other metrics meet thresholds).
- Safety/regression checks: no new PII leakage incidents; toxicity delta <= 1.5 points on our toxic-scan rubric.

Notes on methodology and reproducibility:
- We'll capture random seeds, tokenizer versions, and quantization flags in the run metadata.
- Prompt sets are attached (novus_eval_prompts.csv) and the driver script will pin deterministic sampling (top-p and temperature tied to seed).
- For multi-turn tests we will include utterance-level KV snapshots in the logs (ephemeral; sandbox-only).

Quality regression concerns: if an open model hits metric thresholds but shows systematic failure modes (e.g., consistent hallucination patterns on product-lookup queries), we will flag it for a targeted prompt-engineering pass — not immediate disqualification. Our acceptance rubric includes a "failure-mode basket" where high-severity items (PII leakage, hallucination that leads to wrong billing instructions) are blockers regardless of aggregate metrics.

Deliverables timeline (tentative):
- 2026-06-18: shared prompt set + initial runs (attached).
- 2026-06-20: full benchmark runs in Novus sandbox + dashboard links.
- 2026-06-22: joint review call to inspect samples and reconcile human-annotator labels.

Let us know if Novus wants a tighter human-preference bound (e.g., within 3 points) — we can prioritize extra prompt-scoping.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: baseline-comparison.xlsx, sample_responses_rd.zip
